topic: What is Rust & why learn it

youtube.title: Rust Day 1: Why Learn Rust? (in 60 Seconds) 🦀
youtube.description:
Rust Day 1: What is Rust and why learn it? Here's why developers love it, in 60 seconds.

📌 In this short:
✅ Rust gives you low-level control without the usual hassle
✅ No garbage collector: memory is managed by ownership rules the compiler checks
✅ Great tooling: Cargo, rustfmt and editor support

💻 Code from the video:
fn main() {
    println!("Hello, world!");
}

📖 Learn more: https://doc.rust-lang.org/book/ch00-00-introduction.html
⏭️ Tomorrow: Install Rust & Hello, World!

Follow for a new Rust lesson every day at 6 PM IST, from zero to pro 🦀

sub: Zero to pro, one day at a time
scenes.say: Rust, day one. Why are so many developers learning Rust? Let's find out in sixty seconds.

scenes.heading: Low-level control
scenes.say: Rust helps you write faster, more reliable software. It gives you low-level control, like managing memory, without the usual hassle.

scenes.heading: No garbage collector
scenes.label: rules checked by the compiler
scenes.say: There's no garbage collector. Memory is managed by ownership rules that the compiler checks. Break a rule, and the program won't compile.

scenes.heading: Your first Rust program
scenes.caption: main always runs first
scenes.say: Here's your first program. F N main is where every Rust program starts, and println bang prints a line of text.

scenes.heading: Tooling you'll love
scenes.say: And the tooling is great. Cargo builds your code and manages dependencies, rust format keeps your style consistent, and your editor shows errors as you type.

scenes.heading: Recap
scenes.say: Quick recap: Rust is fast and reliable, memory safe without a garbage collector, and its compiler catches bugs early.

scenes.heading: Day 1 ✓
